chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn Mahbub) from Fadala from al-'Ala' from Muhammad (ibn al-Hajjaj) from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who calls the Adhan while walking, or on the back of his mount, and is not in a state of ritual purity (non-mustahabb to be in a state of purity for the call itself, i.e., not required to be in wudu for the Adhan itself but the question implies the state of the caller). He said: 'If the Tashahhud (sitting for the final testimony) is facing the Qibla, then there is no objection (it is permissible).'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: The sitting portion of the Adhan where the testimony of faith is recited
key_terms.غَيْرِ طَهُورٍ: Not in a state of ritual purity (wudu)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to call the Adhan while walking or riding, and does one need to be in a state of ritual purity?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the flexibility in the physical state of the Mu'adhdhin, distinguishing between the general act of calling and the specific moment of the Tashahhud. It reflects the Shia juristic view that ritual purity (taharah) is not a strict condition for the validity of the Adhan itself, but rather for the solemn declaration of faith within it. This ruling underscores the practical ease (rukhas) granted to the caller in various circumstances, such as riding or walking, while maintaining reverence at the core testimony.
